title: PR shepherd loop
summary: A shepherd session MUST watch one operator-named pull request in bounded windows, decide every feedback item as actioned or rejected in a durable ledger, judge bot feedback against that bot's own review history, implement only accepted items, push only changes a scoped review squad has passed, and answer each decided item on the PR.
instructions: A poll cycle reads the PR's reviews, inline review comments, and conversation comments, then waits about 60 seconds. A watch window runs at least 15 cycles and closes only at quiescence: one full cycle with no new feedback after the window's floor is met. A session MUST run at most 8 windows.

A window that collects no feedback ends the session, and so does a window whose entire batch is rejected. The shepherd MUST assess a non-empty batch only after its window reaches quiescence, never item by item as feedback arrives.

The shepherd MUST record every feedback item in the session ledger when it arrives, with its author, creation time, and URL. Before the session ends, each item MUST hold a final decision: actioned, with the SHA of the pushed commit that carries the fix, or rejected, with its reason. An item that needs an operator decision is put to the operator, and the operator's answer decides it.

Unless the operator directs otherwise, the shepherd MUST treat the feedback that exists on the PR at invocation as batch 0. It MUST assess, implement, review, push, and answer batch 0 before the first watch window opens. Batch 0 does not count against the window limit, and a fully rejected batch 0 does not end the session. An item on a resolved review thread, or one the PR author already answered, is seeded as history and gets no decision.

Before judging a bot's item, the shepherd MUST re-read that bot's ledger history and apply bot discipline: re-apply prior dispositions to repeated items, and reject self-contradictions unless verification favors the newer claim. It MUST reject findings induced by the bot's own earlier accepted item, rather than revert them. It MUST resolve inter-bot conflicts on the merits, and record the losing side. The shepherd MUST NOT implement and later revert the same edit within a session.

The shepherd MUST verify an accepted item against the current code before implementation. Accepted items are implemented as the smallest coherent change with proportionate automated tests under the engineering guidance in force.

The shepherd MUST gate each batch's change through the local review squad, by delegating one pan-shepherd-reviewer subagent with an exact dimension selection. When the operator named dimensions, that set is the selection for every batch. Otherwise the shepherd selects only the dimensions where a defect in the batch could have a material consequence for the PR. It records a reason for each dimension it left out. The subagent runs the selected dimensions per the referenced squad guidance and edits nothing. A batch that still fails after 3 implement-review iterations ends the session with nothing pushed.

Invocation of /pan-shepherd authorizes commits and pushes to the shepherded PR's head branch only, and only for changes whose review passed. It also authorizes one reply to each decided feedback item. The shepherd MUST NOT merge, close, retarget, or rebase the PR. It MUST NOT force-push or push to any other branch, and MUST NOT post any other PR comment unless the operator directed it.

The shepherd MUST answer each decided item on the PR. An actioned reply is exactly `Fixed in <sha>`, posted only after the push that carries that commit. A rejected reply gives one concise reason that names the flaw in the feedback's assumptions or reasoning, the PR's scope, or the risk assessment. A reply MUST follow the writing rules of COMMS-001. It MUST NOT elaborate past that reason, expose the shepherd's reasoning process, refer to the PR author in the third person, or @mention any user.

The shepherd MUST keep a decision table with one row per decided or open item: reviewer, timestamp, comment link, decision, and decision detail, which is the commit SHA or the rejection reason. It MUST post the refreshed table to operator chat each time a row is added or changes.

Every session MUST end with one operator-facing report. The report covers windows used, the final decision table, pushes with SHAs, and review iterations with the dimensions each review ran. It also covers recorded bot contradictions and thrash, and the ledger path.
